title: Ensemble executor chooser with regret-binning for sequence-aware kernel selection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Develop an online, lightweight ensemble-based executor chooser that selects between multiple attention and compute kernels at request time using sequence-length and architecture fingerprints. The chooser should minimize latency tail and cost by using regret-binning and safety fallbacks, while remaining rollout-friendly for Dedicated and Hosted modes.
background: Current heuristics rely on static seqlen buckets or heavy microprofilers, which perform poorly on mixed workloads and heterogeneous hardware. We need a low-overhead runtime decision layer that adapts quickly to workload shifts without destabilizing SLOs.
proposal: Implement an ensemble chooser that keeps per-(arch,fingerprint,seqlen-bin) rolling stats and picks kernels via a regret-binning scoring function. Use controlled probes for cold buckets, decay stale stats, and suspend candidates that violate safety signals.
design_notes: Fingerprint composed of: arch family, cuda compute capability or CPU tier, memory tier, quantization profile
Non-uniform seqlen bucketing derived from traffic histogram (examples: 1-12,13-48,49-192,193-1024)
Regret-binning maintains last-N samples per candidate and computes empirical regret versus best observed
Candidate ensemble: short-seq dense kernel, block-sparse attention, quantized path, and a safe reference kernel
Probe policy: cap probes to 1-3% per cold bucket and add per-GPU probe budget to avoid allocation spikes
Safety: suspend candidate when latency or error rate exceeds thresholds for consecutive probes
acceptance_criteria: Module behind feature flag and toggleable per-route
P95 latency reduction >=5% on mixed-length internal benchmark compared to baseline
No increase in error rate or OOM incidents during 48-hour canary
Telemetry includes per-(fingerprint,bucket) decision events, rewards, and probe counts
Confluence doc and rollout guide published
implementation_plan: Prototype chooser and in-memory stats store (2 weeks)
Instrument seqlen histogram and propose bucket boundaries (3 days)
Integrate chooser into prefill/decode scheduler behind flag (1 week)
Canary on low-volume routes and collect telemetry (1 week)
Iterate on bucket boundaries and probe rates, then staged rollout (2 weeks)
rollout_plan: Start at 1% traffic on non-critical routes for 24 hours
If stable, increase to 10% and monitor for 72 hours
Enable for Dedicated pools with customer opt-in and opt-out circuit-breakers
Require two successful 10% ramps and postmortem review before full enablement
telemetry: Decision event: timestamp | route | fingerprint | bucket | chosen_candidate
Reward event: latency_ms | tokens | cost_estimate | success_flag
Dashboards: per-candidate latency distribution by bucket and architecture
risks: Exploration may increase latency for tail-sensitive routes if probe caps are misconfigured
Fingerprint cardinality could explode — requires rollup and compression
Poor bucket boundaries can bias decisions and reduce effectiveness
Telemetry must avoid any customer-identifying data in fingerprints to prevent leaks
